A.title: Keep Thames Water private, but tie bosses' pay and fines to rivers
A.answer: Keep the owners and the court rescue. Change the rules attached to it. First, the regulator must ban bonuses and dividends until spills fall for three years running, since part of 2025's fall was dry weather (s5). Second, bosses' pay is held back and can be clawed back if the company breaks the rules. Third, the £122.7m fine is paid in full on its backstop date and not written down (s6). Fourth, a new customer panel gets a seat and a veto on bill rises. Bills do not rise to pay the debts. Ofwat does this. We would know it worked if spills keep falling in wet years and no bonus is paid.

B.title: Hand Thames Water to its customers and staff, with debts written down
B.answer: Put Thames Water into special administration, so a court-appointed administrator runs it while its debts are sorted out (s9 argues this can cost close to zero in law). Then move it into a public-benefit company. Customers and staff elect a board, with seats for river groups. Bosses who broke the rules answer for it, and creditors take the loss before any taxpayer does. Bills do not rise to pay old debts. Government does this, with the court hearing on 27 November (s1) as the first step. It worked if spills keep falling in a normal-weather year (s5), the £122.7m fine is paid (s6), and bills stay flat.
